requirements.evidence: Most pieces exist (IssueTicket.php:20-49, enums, exception, Queue model, migrations), but the core path is broken: the tickets migration has no timestamps (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000002_create_tickets_table.php:14-25) while Ticket keeps Eloquent timestamps on, so Ticket::create()/save() insert created_at/updated_at into missing columns; call() is typed App\Models\User at app/Models/Ticket.php:79 which PHP resolves to App\Models\App\Models\User; Ticket::factory()->create() leaves code null (database/factories/TicketFactory.php:21); Entity::queues() is absent; no unique-collision retry (IssueTicket.php:49).

conventions.evidence: Follows several conventions: domain write in app/Actions/IssueTicket.php, migrations with reversible down(), fillable lists declared (Queue.php:12, Ticket.php:15), docs touched (docs/business-rules.md:72-74). Deviations: no tests despite 'no production code without a test', no CHANGELOG entry, and the schema doc change only adds two duplicated/misplaced comments (docs/database-schema.md:110-112).

security.evidence: app/Models/Ticket.php:79-88 call() changes status/called_at/called_by_user_id and saves without any check that $user is a member of the ticket's entity, and never throws AuthorizationException; this is the unauthorized-write anchor. Mass-assignment safety itself is fine: explicit fillable lists at Queue.php:12 and Ticket.php:15.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains only app/, database/ and docs/ files; there is no tests/ file at all, so none of the issuance, nextCode, immutability, single-call or authorization paths are covered.

simplicity.evidence: Implementation is direct and small: one invokable action (IssueTicket.php:20-49), one model method per behaviour, no service/repository layers. Minor waste: nextCode loads every code for the queue into PHP then loops (Ticket.php:57-68), and there are redundant imports.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are short, but app/Models/Ticket.php:11-12 imports DB and Log without using them, Queue.php:9-10 re-imports same-namespace models and Queue.php:31 uses an inline FQCN, Ticket.php:79 uses the namespace-relative FQCN that causes the TypeError, and the schema doc repeats the same 'unique per queue' comment twice (docs/database-schema.md:110,112).

scope.evidence: Every file and edit maps to task.md: models/enums/exception/action/factories/migrations plus the two explicitly requested docs (docs/business-rules.md:72-74, docs/database-schema.md:110-112). No unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The tickets table has no created_at/updated_at columns, but Ticket does not disable Eloquent timestamps, so both Ticket::create() in IssueTicket and Ticket::call() will attempt to insert/update missing columns and fail.

The parameter type App\Models\User inside namespace App\Models resolves to App\Models\App\Models\User (verified with PHP reflection), so call() cannot be invoked with a normal User and will raise a TypeError.

call() performs the state change and save without authorizing that the caller belongs to the ticket's entity, so any user could call any ticket; the task requires AuthorizationException for non-members.

The default state sets code to null and only forQueue() allocates a code, so Ticket::factory()->create() inserts NULL into the NOT NULL code column instead of allocating the next per-queue code as the contract requires.
The contract requires App\Models\Entity::queues() (hasMany), but the Entity model is not modified and no queues() relation appears anywhere in the diff.

DB::transaction(..., 3) retries only deadlock/concurrency errors, not a unique (queue_id, code) violation, so the explicitly required collision retry is not implemented (the queue row lock mitigates it but does not fulfil the requirement).

nextCode takes the numeric maximum rather than the last valid code in insertion order, so deleting the highest ticket (A001..A003, delete A003) yields A003 again, contrary to 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'; it also loads all queue codes into PHP.

No Pest/PHPUnit tests were added for any new behaviour, including the required authorization failure, immutability, single-call and code-generation edge cases, violating the project's test-driven convention.

The schema doc only gains two comments on the same field (one of them misplaced after priority) and uses '//' inside what appears to be a Mermaid ER diagram; the new queue table and ticket call columns are not documented.
The conventions require a Keep a Changelog entry under [Unreleased] for a user-visible change, but no CHANGELOG edit is included.
Unused DB/Log imports, redundant same-namespace imports and an inline fully-qualified BelongsTo return type add noise and differ from the surrounding style.

review.summary: The change adds the queue/ticket schema, models, enums, exception, factories and an IssueTicket action, but the persistence path cannot work as written because the tickets migration omits timestamps while Eloquent still manages them, and Ticket::call() has both a namespace-resolution bug and no entity-membership authorization. Together with the broken default factory, missing Entity::queues() and the total absence of tests, this needs substantial rework before it can be approved.
